question.text: The <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>H</mi></math> amount of thermal energy is developed by a resistor in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> when a current of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> is passed through it. If the current is increased to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>16</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math>, the thermal energy developed by the resistor in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> will be

solution.text:
Heat energy developed in the resistor due to current is given by, H=i2Rt. Therefore 

⇒H∝i2 (for t= constant)

Now required ratio, HH'=4162

⇒H'=16H
